title: Aramid Fibres: Kevlar
welcome_lead: Bulletproof, tough, and stronger than steel by weight.
meta_desc: A-Level D&T: aramid fibres, Kevlar, and ballistic textiles.
final_note: Five times stronger than steel by weight.

walkthroughs.body_html: Stephanie Kwolek, working at DuPont in 1965, discovered the aramid fibre marketed from 1971 as Kevlar. She received the Lemelson-MIT Prize and the National Medal of Technology.
Kevlar fibres reach tensile strength of about 3600 MPa at density 1440 kg/m^3 — roughly 5 times the specific strength of steel. Used in body armour, ropes, sails, racing tyres.
Kevlar is woven into vests, used as reinforcement in aramid-CFRP hybrids, and as honeycomb cores. Nomex, its meta-aramid sibling (introduced 1967), is heat-resistant for firefighter and racing suits.
